newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down led by construction shares.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down led by construction shares.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended down on Friday after the construction sector came under heavy fire due to rumours about the financial stability of Tobishima Corp, which the firm later denied, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended down 171.39 points, or 0.95 percent, at 17,867.04. Its March futures were down 170 points at 17,860.
"Persisting worries about the financial state of sectors groaning under the weight of bad loans took their toll once again," said Akihiro Naemura, an analyst at Okasan Securities.
Stocks were initially boosted by a rally in global blue chips, such as Sony Corp, but upward momentum was halted by heavy selling in property-related issues.

During the afternoon, Tobishima fell to a limit-low of 121 yen due to rumours that it might be applying for court protection from its creditors. Tobishima denied the rumour and Fuji Bank Ltd, a major creditor bank, said that a restructuring programme for the firm was making progress, but the selling continued. Tobishima ended down 40 yen at 161.
Losers outdid winners 781 issues to 281, while 169 issues were unchanged.
Turnover ballooned to 506 million shares from 393 million on the previous day, as troubled issues, such as hotelier Gajoen Kanko KK and sushi chain operator Kyotaru Co Ltd, dominated trade.
While the market was also preoccupied with the construction sector, the yen slipped to the 124 level.
"Investors believe a weaker yen will boost the performance of export-related firms, especially bellwether issues," said Keiko Kondo, a strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.
"But attention seems to be more on Japan's financial worries than currencies at the moment."
Brokers added that further weakening of the yen was likely and buyers were not in a hurry to scoop up export-issues.
The upcoming meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations on Saturday and market holiday on Tuesday, encouraged market participants to keep positions short, they said.
Toyota Motor Corp surged 60 yen to 3,160 yen on news that it would resume production after a fire last weekend halted component supplier Aisin Seiki Co Ltd.
Sumitomo Metal Mining Co added 13 yen to 784, after news that a U.S. subsidiary may have a potential gold mine in Alaska, brokers said.
Most construction firms fell. Fujita Corp shed 18 yen to 193 and was the sixth most active issue in trade of 6.279 million shares. Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd fell 24 yen to 207.
Brokerages 0#SEC.T topped the loser-by-section list. Nikko Securities Co Ltd was down 30 yen at 674. Nomura Securities Co Ltd fell 20 yen to 1,500.
Other declining sectors were real estate, electric power, gas and mining. Gainers were led by shipbuilding, automobile, precision instruments and pulp/paper.
Other indices were also lower, with the TOPIX down 8.38 points, or 0.62 percent, at 1,341.50. The Nikkei 300 average lost 1.30 points, or 0.51 percent, to 255.79.
The second section index was down 12.61 points, or 0.73 percent, at 1,718.74. Its turnover was 8.21 million shares against Thursday's 7.86 million.
In late Tokyo, the over-the-counter index was down 11.67 points, or 0.92 percent, at 1,255.40.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
